item.title: MCUboot vs OpenBLT vs TinyUF2 in 2026: Secure Firmware Updates for Microcontrollers Compared
item.description: A product without a field update path has a maintenance model built on truck rolls. The moment a fleet of deployed devices needs a bug fix, the bootloader you chose two years earlier becomes the most expensive code in the project — and the one you can never change afterwards, because a failed bootloader update bricks hardware in the field.

item.title: Self-Hosted Linux Bootloader Management: GRUB vs systemd-boot vs rEFInd
item.description: The bootloader is the first piece of software that runs when a Linux server starts — it loads the kernel, passes boot parameters, and hands control to the operating system. While many administrators never think about their bootloader until something goes wrong, choosing the right one affects boot reliability, security, multi-boot capability, and recovery options.
